answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded natural-language answer to "Is the relation between socioeconomic status and chances of degree completion affected by racial lines of the individual?"):

"SES is positively associated with BA-degree completion within every racial group in this NLS sample (n = 8,773; 236 completions), but the strength of that association does not differ significantly across racial lines on the relative (odds) scale: after controlling for sex and family size, the SES log-odds slope is statistically indistinguishable between White respondents (OR 1.74), Black respondents (OR 1.74 × e^0.31 ≈ 2.37, interaction p = 0.09) and Hispanic respondents (OR 1.74 × e^0.11 ≈ 1.95, p = 0.63), with the two interactions jointly non-significant (LR χ²(2) = 2.58, p = 0.28) and per-race stratified fits statistically equal (SES ORs 1.82 / 2.18 / 1.82; equality Wald tests p ≥ 0.33). What racial lines do change is the payoff in absolute probability: because baseline completion is far lower for Black (1.3%) and Hispanic (1.4%) than White (3.5%) respondents, a one-SD SES advantage raises predicted completion probability by only ~0.9–1.0 percentage points for Black and Hispanic respondents versus ~2.3 points for White respondents (bootstrap 95% CIs for the minority-minus-White contrasts exclude zero: [−2.15, −0.84] and [−2.16, −0.73] pp). Net of the SES-linked academic-resources pathway (composite ASVAB and class percentile, model M3), the SES gradient shrinks for all groups (≈0.2–0.6 pp per SD) and the negative racial main effects disappear (Black even reverses sign), indicating that ability and class standing are the principal channel through which SES and race jointly affect degree completion. Thus, racial lines affect the SES→degree relation mainly by lowering the baseline and hence the absolute return to SES for Black and Hispanic respondents — not through a detectably different relative SES slope — though with only 19–28 completion events in the minority groups, modest slope differences cannot be ruled out."

KEY RESULTS (M2 headline: logit BA ~ SES + race + SES×race + sex + family size, HC1 robust SEs):
- M1 (no controls): SES 0.161 (p=.03); ses×Black +0.565 (p=.002), ses×Hisp +0.338 (p=.088) — raw interaction significant for Black, but confounded by family structure (family size is a strong suppressor).
- M2 (headline): SES +0.554 (OR 1.74, p<.001); ses×Black +0.306 (p=.094); ses×Hisp +0.112 (p=.628); male −0.247 (p=.067); family size −0.610 (p<.001). Joint interaction LRT p=0.275.
- M3 (labeled comparison, net of academic resources): SES +0.175 (p=.084); ses×Black +0.272 (p=.184); ses×Hisp +0.011 (p=.964); ASVAB z +0.845 (p<.001); class percentile +2.36 (p<.001); race main effects turn positive/non-negative.
- Marginal effects (M2, delta-method SEs): AME of +1 SD SES on P(BA): White +2.33 pp [1.80, 2.86]; Black +0.90 pp [0.49, 1.31]; Hispanic +0.99 pp [0.40, 1.57]. In M3 these fall to +0.58 / +0.23 / +0.24 pp (minority CIs include 0).
- Predicted P(BA) at SES 25th/50th/75th percentiles (M2): White 2.3/3.1/4.3%; Black 0.9/1.2/1.7%; Hispanic 1.2/1.6/2.3%.

ROBUSTNESS CHECKS (all in outputs/analysis_report.txt):
- R1 Linear probability model (HC1): SES +1.09 pp (p<.001); ses×Black +0.12 pp (p=.82), ses×Hisp −0.46 pp (p=.30) — no significant additive-scale interaction; same sign as the logit AME contrast but imprecise, so the additive-scale evidence is mixed and I flag it in the caveats.
- R2a Cubic in SES: interactions essentially unchanged (ses×Black +0.325, p=.086).
- R2b SES standardized within race: ses×Black +0.177 (p=.25), ses×Hisp +0.181 (p=.46) — confirms the M1 uncontrolled interaction partly reflected cross-group SES distribution differences, and that after controls the relative slopes are similar.
- R3 Firth penalized logit (hand-implemented, 13 iters): coefficients nearly identical to M2 (ses×Black +0.313, p=.092) — no rare-event bias correction changes the conclusion.
- R4 Stratified fits + cross-equation Wald: SES ORs 1.82 (White, p<.001), 2.18 (Black, p<.001), 1.82 (Hispanic, p=.004); equality tests White=Black p=.33, White=Hispanic p=.99, Black=Hispanic p=.50.
- R5 Bootstrap (1,000 reps, seed 20261019) of the AME contrast (minority − White): Black [−2.15, −0.84] pp; Hispanic [−2.16, −0.73] pp.

ASSUMPTIONS AND LIMITATIONS (phrased conditionally in the hypothesis): (1) the follow-up window defining "BA completed" is not documented, so the hypothesis is phrased without asserting a timing; (2) no sampling weights are supplied (if this is an NLSY-style survey with minority oversamples, unweighted estimates describe the processed sample, not the population); (3) the outcome is rare (2.7%) with only 19–28 minority-group events, so interaction power is limited and the additive-scale evidence is mixed (logit AME contrast significant, LPM interaction not); (4) ability/rank were treated as part of the SES pathway per the researcher's direction, with M3 shown only as the labeled net-of-resources comparison; (5) observational data — all statements are associations, not causal effects.

WORKFLOW DESCRIPTION (for submission): loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows × 8 cols, zero missing, zero duplicate CASE IDs); verified SES is continuous (5,753 distinct values, range −2.45..2.72), race has 3 levels (White 5,337 / Black 2,113 / Hispanic 1,323), outcome has 236 positives; standardized SES and the ASVAB composite, scaled class percentile to [0,1]; fit M1/M2/M3 logistic regressions with SES×race interactions and HC1 robust SEs; computed average marginal effects of +1 SD SES within each race via the delta method and percentile bootstrap (1,000 reps) for the racial contrasts; ran robustness checks: linear probability model, cubic SES, SES standardized within race, Firth penalized logit, per-race stratified fits with cross-equation Wald tests; saved the full report to outputs/analysis_report.txt.

payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows × 8 columns; zero missing values, zero duplicate CASE IDs). Verified SES is continuous (5,753 distinct values, range −2.45..2.72; not banded), race has 3 levels (White 5,337 / Black 2,113 / Hispanic 1,323), sex is binary, and BA DEGREE COMPLETED has 236 positives (2.69%). Standardized SES and the ASVAB composite and scaled class percentile to [0,1]. Fit three nested logistic regressions (M1: SES+race+SES×race; M2: +sex+family size — headline; M3: +ASVAB z +class percentile — labeled net-of-academic-resources comparison) with HC1 robust SEs, plus a joint LR test of the interactions. Estimated average marginal effects of +1 SD SES within each race by the delta method and percentile bootstrap (1,000 reps, fixed seed) for racial contrasts, and predicted probabilities at SES quartiles. Robustness: linear probability model; cubic SES; SES standardized within race; Firth penalized logit (rare-event check); per-race stratified logits with cross-equation Wald equality tests. Treated ability/class rank as part of the SES pathway per study direction. All estimates are observational associations; unweighted (no weights supplied); follow-up timing undocumented.
